Frameworks change monthly. Each encodes: A new framework has arrived every year since 2022. Each encodes a theory of where control lives: your code, the model, the vendor's harness, or a graph you draw. You choose that theory and defend it.
Workflow: the model runs along code path: A workflow runs the model along code paths you wrote. An agent lets the model direct its own control flow. Anthropic's advice: use a workflow wherever the path is known in advance, and the open loop only where it is not.

Fixed sequence; each step's output is th: A fixed sequence. Each step's output is the next step's input, with an optional gate between steps.
Classify the input, dispatch to a specia: A classifier sorts each input and dispatches it to a specialized path.
Sectioning (split, run, merge) or voting: Sectioning splits the task, runs the parts, and merges the results. Voting runs the same task N times and aggregates the answers.
One model produces, another critiques, l: One model produces, another critiques, and the pair loops until the criteria are met.
Open loop: model plans, acts on tools, o: The open loop: the model plans, acts on tools, observes, and continues until it is done or halted.

Card 2's discipline: hold the tool layer: Card 2 holds the tool layer constant so that the pattern is the only variable. The delta is then attributable to the decision recorded in ADR-1.
The abstraction tax: every layer a frame: Every layer a framework adds is a layer you cannot see into during Drift (the abstraction tax). If you cannot explain what the framework did on turn three, you do not own the loop.
Chains, agents, tools, memory as objects: LangChain wrapped the ReAct prompt in objects (chains, agents, tools, memory). The wrapper made the loop importable and also hid it, so practitioners paid the abstraction tax in opaque prompts and release-to-release drift.
The agent as a state graph: nodes are st: LangGraph models the agent as a state graph. Nodes are steps, edges are control flow you draw, state is typed, checkpoints persist it, and a human interrupt is an edge. You own every edge.
Every output is validated against a Pyda: Pydantic AI validates every model output against a Pydantic model before the output acts, and retries or rejects a malformed one.
